texts.facts: 2. By filing this CAN 1 of 2026, in the instant Public Interest Litigation (WPA (P) 153 of 2025), the petitioners have highlighted the incident of riot Suvendu Adhikari & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28017528/ 2 and damage to public property targeting a community etc., which had taken place on 16/17.01.2026. In the relief, it is prayed for issuing immediate directions for deployment of Central Forces in and around area of Beldanga, 3 Murshidabad and the adjoining areas in the light of previous directions issued by this Court in the instant matter on 12.04.2025. Secondly, it is prayed that an enquiry/investigation be directed to be conducted by respondent no.5 in order to apprise the Court about recurring incidents of communal violence, arson, destruction of public and private property and disruption of public infrastructure in the District of Murshidabad, West Bengal and other border areas. 3. Lastly, it is prayed to pass an order promulgating prohibitory orders under Section 163 of B.N.S.S., 2023 without further delay.
texts.arguments: 4. Sri Billwadal Bhattacharya, learned senior counsel submits that on 16.01.2026, sizeable number of persons were protesting against the death of migrant worker in Jharkhand. On the next day, the mob used force and damaged public property, assaulted the Government officials and the police personnel. They were armed with various kinds of weapons. This act falls within the ambit of a "terrorist act", as envisaged in Section 15 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (hereinafter referred to as "U.A.P.A. Act"). By taking this Court to Chapter - III Section 6 of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 (hereinafter referred to as "NIA Act") coupled with the Entry - II of the Schedule appended to the Act it is argued that it is the statutory obligation on the part of the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station to receive the information under Section 154 of the Cr.P.C. and in turn, forward the report to the State Government forthwith. On receipt of such report, the State Government is also under an obligation to mandatorily forward the report to the Central Government as expeditiously as possible. By placing reliance on Sub-Section 5 of Section 6, Sri Bhattacharya submits that a non obstante clause is put in the opening of Sub- Section 5, which makes it clear that Central Government has independent and suo motu power to look into the matter and direct agency to investigate any offence covered under the NIA Act. Suvendu Adhikari & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28017528/ 3 5. It is submitted that earlier this Court in the instant matter passed a detailed order when the violence broke out on 11th April, 2025. This Court passed certain directions and in order to bolster the same, reliance is placed on paragraphs 16 and 18 of the said order. It is submitted that a plain reading of paragraph 15, 25, 31 and 32 of the PIL will make it clear that the present incident of violence at Beldanga is in continuation of the earlier incident and cannot be seen as an isolated incident. 6. Sri Bhattacharya further submits that the assembly of 100 persons with arms, assault on police, damage of public property and vandalism is highly objectionable. It is further canvassed that the district Murshidabad connects the North Bengal with South Bengal. Thus, its position is very crucial and in the instant matter, National Highway No.12, which passes through Mursdhibdad was disrupted, which resulted into stoppage of food supply and other materials. Considering this grave situation, the State Government ought to have utilized the Central Armed Forces available in the area and Central Government should have also examined whether there exists a need of deployment of further armed forces. Both the Governments need to protect the life of the people. 7. Sri Kalyan Bandyopadhyay, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Sirsanya Bandyopadhyay, learned Senior Standing Counsel for the State submits that this PIL was arising out of an incident, which had taken place on 11.04.2025. This cannot be connected with the present incident of violence at Beldanga. It is further submitted that the relief prayed in I.A. No. CAN 1 of 2026 is not connected with the main relief prayed for in the PIL. 8. The newspaper report on which Sri Billwadal Bhattacharya, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has relied upon during the course of hearing was referred to by submitting the said news agency has not been impleaded as a party respondent. Although in the said report, it is mentioned that unrest in Beldanga had begun on Friday morning and the incident on the first day was voluntary but on the second day i.e. 17.01.2026 it was a calculated attempt, learned counsel for the State submits that no reliance can be placed in a PIL on a newspaper report. 9. Sri Bandyopadhyay, learned senior counsel submits that life and liberty of citizens is undoubtedly very precious and all possible efforts needs to be taken to protect the said right of the citizens. He has no objection if the Central Armed Forces are utilized to their fullest capacity and if necessary, more number of Central Forces are deployed in the area. 10. Sri Bandyopadhyay, learned senior counsel further submits that after the incident, immediate steps have been taken and 30 persons have already been arrested. FIRs have been lodged. After 16/17.01.2026 when violent incidents have taken place, the situation was brought under control. On 18.01.2026, 19.01.2026 and today, no incident of violence or untoward incident has been reported. He however apprised that public life is now normal in Beldanga and Mursdhidabad. 11. During the course of hearing, learned senior counsel for the State submits that he will file affidavit in opposition within 15 days to apprise the Court about the incident and the action taken thereupon. Suvendu Adhikari & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28017528/ 4 12. Learned Additional Soilicitor General Sri Ashoke Kumar Chakraborty apprised the Court that in Beldanga 5 Companies of B.S.F., in Jangipur Police Station 8 Companies CRPF and in Samshergunge 4 Companies of BSF are existing in compliance of previous order of this Court dated 12.04.2025. 13. By placing heavy reliance on the instructions received, learned Additional Solicitor General urged that although sizeable number of Central Armed Forces were available in the area, their utilization was minimal in nature. It is submitted that on 16.01.2026, B.S.F. was utilized only for 02 hours and on 17.01.2026, Central Force was also utilized only for 1 and hours. The decision to utilize such forces is solely dependant on the requirements shown by the Beldanga Police Station. 14. By taking this Court to the 7th Schedule List I Entry - 2A of the Constitution of India it is submitted that it is the prerogative of the Central Government to deploy the force. State List - II is referred to show that Entry - 2 makes it clear that the police and the deployment of force is subject to provisions of Entry - 2A of the List - I mentioned hereinabove. 15. Next reliance is placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Naga People's Movement of Human Rights vs. Union of India & Ors. reported in (1998) 2 SCC 109. Paragraph 24 is pressed into service to contend that the decision to deploy the Central Forces is the prerogative to the Central Government. 16. Lastly, Sri Chakraborty, learned Additional Solicitor General referred to certain interlocutory orders passed by this Court in W.P.A. (P) 168 of 2024 Vishva Hindu Parishad Dakshinbanga & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Ors. The orders are relied upon to contend that in view of the factual backdrop of the matter, it is the fit case where action under the NIA Act can be taken. 17. In rejoinder submission learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners reiterated his stand and urged that immediate directions needs to be issued to protect the life of the people, which is precious and Constitutionally recognized under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. 18. Sri Kalyan Bandyopadhyay at the cost of repetition, submits that life of the people is very precious and it needs to be protected and on that point, there cannot be any quarrel. However, the incident should not be given a political shape. He undertakes to file affidavit in opposition within 15 days. Mr. Bandyopadhyay submits that Article 355 cannot be invoked unless the State made a request to the Union of India for assistance of police force in maintaining the law and order situation. However, Mr. Bandyopadhyay, has fairly submitted the power of the Court to direct the deployment of CRPF or para-military forces are not curtailed by the said article depending upon the facts situation. He has also fairly submitted that in a given situation the State police and Central Police Forces can act hand in hand to pacify the situation and ensure peaceful co-existence of different communities in the State. 23. The argument advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners is relating to assembly of armed persons in the name of agitation on 16/17.01.2026, assault to the police personnel and the Suvendu Adhikari & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28017528/ 6 Government officials/employees, damage to the property and vandalism etc. In addition, it was highlighted that National Highway No. 12, which is very important in national and defence interest has been blocked. Pertinently, Sri Bandyopadhyay, learned senior counsel has not disputed that such incidents have taken place on 16/17.01.2026. However, his stand was that after 17.01.2026, the condition is under control and no untoward incident had taken place.
